toJSONSchema(schemaRegistry, opts) is very slow with a large registry
raw.body:
As I add more types to a schema registry, calling `toJSONSchema` on that registry gets very slow, growing much faster than the growth in the size of the registry.

In a private repo I have, a registry with only about 3000 types in it takes 30 seconds to process on a MacBook M3.

I've collected some perf dumps, and the problem might be coming from one or both of these places:

### Finalize iteration

`finalize` is called on every schema, but for each schema it goes through all of the refs and checks each one:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L449

A lot of that ends up being noop, as everything only needs to be procesesd once.  But it's still building all of those new arrays for iteration and revisiting every member of `ctx.seen` many times over.

When I hack my copy of zod to only run this loop once per context, the schema generation time for my example goes down from about 30s to about 18s.

### Nested parent computation

When a schema has a parent, registry get walks the chain recursively to get ancestor data:

raw.title: ability to define inline non-empty array which is expressed in its inferred type (in v4)
raw.body:
## Feature request
The change in `z.array()`'s `.nonempty()` between zod v3 and v4 (see [migration guide](https://zod.dev/v4/changelog?id=changes-nonempty-type#changes-nonempty-type)) causes the inferred type to no longer express that the array contains at least one element `T[]` vs. `[T, ...T[]]`.

The proposed solution in the migration guide is to use `z.tuple([elementSchema], elementSchema)`. Please note that this requires to repeat the element schema. In case it's a non-trivial element schema, it's hard to read and maintain in case it is defined inline. Essentially, this forces the element schema to be stored non-inline, in a variable, which also impacts readability.

I'd like to request the feature to be able to define a schema for a non-empty array inline, without repeating the element schema.

## Related tickets
There are already 2 issues about this change in inferred type:
* https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/5253
* https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4888

Please note that the feature request in my issue is not necessarily about the change in inferred type, but about the ability to define an (inline) schema for non-empty arrays without repeating the element's sub-schema.

## Proposed solution options
* Change the inferred type of `z.array()`'s `.nonempty()` from `T[]` to `T[] & [T, ...T[]]`.
* Add a new function to `z.array()`, e.g. `.withAtLeastOneElement()` which behaves like `.nonempty()`, but having inferred type   `T[] & [T, ...T[]]`.
* Introduce a helper, e.g. `z.nonEmptyArray(elementSchema)`, which will behave the same as
  * either: `z.array(elementSchema).nonempty()`, but then with the inferred type of `T[] & [T, ...T[]]` or just `[T, ...T[]]`
  * or: `z.tuple([elementSchema], elementSchema)`

raw.title: treeifyError throws TypeError when an issue path contains a key inherited from Object.prototype (e.g. toString)
raw.body:
`treeifyError` throws a `TypeError` whenever a validation issue's `path` contains a segment whose name matches a property inherited from `Object.prototype` (for example `toString`, `valueOf`, `constructor`, or `hasOwnProperty`).

Minimal reproduction:

```
import zod, { treeifyError } from 'zod';

const schema = zod.object({ toString: zod.string() });
const result = schema.safeParse({}); // success: false

if (!result.success) {
    treeifyError(result.error); // throws TypeError
}
```

The parse correctly fails: `{}.toString` resolves to the inherited `Object.prototype.toString` function, so the `toString` field is reported as `invalid_type (expected string, received function)` with `path: ["toString"]`. That part is expected. The bug is that `treeifyError` then throws while building the tree:

```
node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113
                        curr.errors.push(mapper(issue));
                                    ^
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
    at processError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113:37)
    at treeifyError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:120:5)
```

Root cause:

`treeifyError` builds the tree using a plain object as a dictionary:

```
curr.properties ?? (curr.properties = {});
(_a = curr.properties)[el] ?? (_a[el] = { errors: [] });
curr = curr.properties[el];
```

When the path segment `el` is an `Object.prototype` key, `curr.properties[el]` returns the inherited member (e.g. the `toString` function) instead of `undefined`. The `??` short-circuits, so the node is never created, and `curr` is assigned the inherited function which has no `errors` array. The following `curr.errors.push(...)` then throws.
A null-prototype object (`Object.create(null)`) or a `Map` for `properties`, or an `Object.hasOwn` guard, would fix it.

Environment:
zod: 4.4.3
Node.js: v24.15.0

regexes.domain is missing RFC 1035 length limits
raw.body:
## Context

`regexes.domain` (used by `z.httpUrl()` for the URL host check) currently has no length anchors:

```ts
export const domain: RegExp = /^([a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/;
```

vs. `regexes.hostname` (used by `z.hostname()`), which does enforce the RFC 1035 limits:

```ts
export const hostname: RegExp =
  /^(?=.{1,253}\.?$)[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[-0-9a-zA-Z]{0,61}[0-9a-zA-Z])?)*\.?$/;
```

So `z.httpUrl()` accepts hosts that exceed the 253-character total or have non-TLD labels longer than 63 characters, while `z.hostname()` rejects them.

## Question

Is this an intentional looseness for `z.httpUrl()` (since RFC 3986 / WHATWG URL doesn't itself impose DNS length limits, even though the underlying DNS does), or a gap worth closing?

If the latter, the fix is small — adding a `(?=.{1,253}\.?$)` lookahead and capping the TLD with a `{2,63}` quantifier. Happy to follow up with a PR if there's interest.

## Note

This is independent from #5963 (underscore support, currently open), but it'd be cleaner to land that first to avoid noisy rebases.

raw.title: redos checker test fails on Windows: recheck-jar path uses forward-slash regex on backslash paths
raw.body:
## Summary

`src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts > redos checker` fails on every Windows contributor's machine with:

```
Error: Invalid or corrupt jarfile C:\Users\<…>\node_modules\recheck-jar\package.json
```

Linux CI is green; the bug is purely platform-specific path handling in `recheck`'s self-resolution logic.

## Reproduction

- Windows 10 / 11
- Any Node version
- Clean clone of zod, `pnpm install`, then:

```sh
pnpm vitest run src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts -t "redos checker"
```

Result: test fails (or times out) with the "Invalid or corrupt jarfile" error above.

## Root cause

`recheck` (the library used to assert no ReDoS-vulnerable patterns) resolves both its native binary and its bundled jar using:

```ts
require.resolve(pkg).replace(/\/package\.json$/, "/<bin>")
```

The forward-slash regex silently no-ops on Windows, where `require.resolve` returns a backslash path. `recheck` then spawns Java/exe with `package.json` itself as the executable argument — hence the corrupt-jar error.

The test itself is correct; the failure is in the optional-dependency resolution shape inside `recheck`.

## Proposed fix

[#5919](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5919) registers a small `scripts/recheck-resolve.ts` ahead of `fail-on-console` in the vitest configs. It uses `path.join` (separator-correct on every platform) to resolve:

- `recheck-{platform}-{arch}/recheck[.exe]` → exported as `RECHECK_BIN` (the native-backend override)
- `recheck-jar/recheck.jar` → exported as `RECHECK_JAR` (JVM fallback)

`recheck` short-circuits its own (buggy) resolution when either env var is set, so this is a transparent override. Pure test-infra change — no production code touched. Skips on platforms without an installed `recheck-{platform}-{arch}` or `recheck-jar` package (e.g. s390x, riscv64, FreeBSD).

## Related (different cause, same test)

These touch the same `redos checker` test but at different layers, so this issue is not a duplicate:

- #5365 — Node 22 regex engine throws a ReDoS issue inside `recheck` (closed not-planned).
- #5743 — Node 24 V8 regex perf makes the test exceed 5s timeout (closed via timeout bump).

This issue is the third axis: Windows-specific path resolution inside `recheck`'s optional-dep loader.

raw.title: z.email() should restrict length to 254 characters
raw.body:
Admittedly this is in the dark recesses of IETF errata but, in accepted errata for RFC 3696, emails should not exceed 254 characters: https://www.rfc-editor.org/errata_search.php?rfc=3696

> In addition to restrictions on syntax, there is a length limit on
   email addresses.  That limit is a maximum of 64 characters (octets)
   in the "local part" (before the "@") and a maximum of 255 characters
   (octets) in the domain part (after the "@") for a total length of 320
   characters. However, there is a restriction in RFC 2821 on the length of an
   address in MAIL and RCPT commands of 254 characters.  Since addresses
   that do not fit in those fields are not normally useful, the upper
   limit on address lengths should normally be considered to be 254.


RFC 3696 is for the [checking and transformation of names](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3696) and includes a section on [email validation](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3696#section-3) which in the non-corrected version says:

>   In addition to restrictions on syntax, there is a length limit on
   email addresses.  That limit is a maximum of 64 characters (octets)
   in the "local part" (before the "@") and a maximum of 255 characters
   (octets) in the domain part (after the "@") for a total length of 320
   characters.  Systems that handle email should be prepared to process
   addresses which are that long, even though they are rarely
   encountered.

So: the original limit was 320, the corrected limit is 254. Right now ZodEmail is defined as a [regex](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/c7805073fef5b6b8857307c3d4b3597a70613bc2/packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts#L452-L458) so (afaict) we'd want a fast length check before running that regex.

[Bug] toJSONSchema crashes on undefined schema inputs in process() and isTransforming()
raw.body:
**Zod version**: 4.3.6 (also reproduced on 4.3.5)
**Related**: #5129 (closed, but bug still present in 4.3.6)

## Description

`process()` and `isTransforming()` in `v4/core/to-json-schema.js` access `schema._zod.def` without null-checking the input. When a record schema has an undefined `valueType` (e.g., from JSON Schema → Zod conversion generating schemas with optional record types), the `recordProcessor` passes `undefined` to these functions, causing a crash.

## Error

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')
    at process (zod/v4/core/to-json-schema.js:33)
```

And after patching `process()`:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')
    at isTransforming (zod/v4/core/to-json-schema.js:365)
```

## Crash Sites

**`process()` — line 33:**
```js
export function process(schema, ctx, _params = { path: [], schemaPath: [] }) {
    var _a;
    // ❌ No null-check — crashes if schema is undefined
    const def = schema._zod.def;
```

**`isTransforming()` — line 365:**
```js
function isTransforming(_schema, _ctx) {
    // ❌ No null-check — crashes if _schema is undefined
    const ctx = _ctx ?? { seen: new Set() };
    // ...
    const def = _schema._zod.def;
```

## Root Cause

The `recordProcessor` in `json-schema-processors.js` calls `process(def.valueType, ...)`. For some record schemas (particularly those generated from JSON Schema → Zod conversion via `json-schema-to-zod`), `def.valueType` can be `undefined`. Similarly, `isTransforming()` recursively processes `def.valueType` for record/map types without checking if it's defined first.

## Reproduction Context

This affects anyone using the MCP (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem with Zod v4:

1. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` calls `toJSONSchema` internally to serialize tool parameter schemas for `tools/list`
2. `@payloadcms/plugin-mcp` uses `json-schema-to-zod` to convert collection JSON Schemas → Zod schemas
3. Some generated Zod record schemas have `undefined` `valueType` in their `_zod.def`
4. `tools/list` → `toJsonSchemaCompat()` → `toJSONSchema()` → `process(undefined)` → crash

## Proposed Fix

Simple null guards at the entry of both functions:

```diff
 export function process(schema, ctx, _params = { path: [], schemaPath: [] }) {
     var _a;
+    if (!schema || !schema._zod) return {};
     const def = schema._zod.def;
```

```diff
 function isTransforming(_schema, _ctx) {
+    if (!_schema || !_schema._zod) return false;
     const ctx = _ctx ?? { seen: new Set() };
```

These are safe defaults — an undefined schema has no JSON Schema representation (empty object) and is not transforming (false).

## Relationship to #5129

Issue #5129 reported the identical crash on v4.0.17 and was closed. However, we've verified the bug still exists in **v4.3.6** — the `to-json-schema.js` source has no null-checks in either function. The only change between 4.3.5 and 4.3.6 in this file is an unrelated `refSeen.def` guard at line 256.

## Impact

This blocks the entire MCP tool listing for any project using `@payloadcms/plugin-mcp` (or any MCP server that generates Zod schemas from JSON Schema) with Zod v4. The `tools/list` response fails completely, making all MCP tools inaccessible. We're currently working around this with `pnpm patch`.

Thanks for the library and all the great work put into it! I get that naming things and keeping things consistent can be daunting, and that's also the origin of my question in this regard:

Currently in our codebase, we're using both `z.infer` and `z.output` and `z.input`. Sometimes, we're changing types, so a type might have the same input and output type and over time will receive a difference on those.

type Equal<A, B> =
  [A] extends [B] ? ([B] extends [A] ? true : false) : false;

  Equal<z.input<S>, z.output<S>> extends true ? z.output<S> : never;

raw.body:
`z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(2.5e-7)` returns `{ success: true }`,  but `2.5e-7 / 1e-7 = 2.5`  (not a whole number).

Repro:
```
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(2.5e-7)  //  { success: true } — should be false
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(3.3e-7)  // { success: true } — should be false
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(3e-7)    // { success: true } — correct
```

Root cause: `floatSafeRemainder` in util.ts counts decimal places by splitting `val.toString()` on ".". For small numbers, JS uses scientific notation: (2.5e-7).toString() gives "2.5e-7", so the fractional part is "5e-7" (length 4) instead of the actual 8 decimal places. 

The function already handles this for the step parameter (lines 251-255) but not for val.

Suggested fix: Apply the same scientific notation regex to val.toString().

Zod version: 4.3.6

raw.body:
We see CSP errors in production builds because Zod checks `new Function("")` to determine whether unsafe-eval is possible. I don't really care that Zod _tries_ to use unsafe-eval, because our policy will disallow it. It being logged is the annoying part. Since these are reported to our violation report endpoint and clutter up (very important) security logs, we consider it a security regression.

In several issues, among which:
- https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4461
- https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/5414

the recommended solution is to set `z.config({ jitless: true })`. This needs to happen _before_ any other imports occur that use Zod, which is problematic in our SPA-case, because this forces me to load and configure Zod before anything else can happen, leading to unnecessary slowdown in startup.

Other solutions, such as re-exporting Zod, are unstable, when considering third party libraries or generated code using regular Zod imports.

The above workaround is also undesirable, because it creates a forced bootstrap/import-order workaround, it introduces an extra loading step / waterfall in app startup, which make it not feel like a long-term solution to this problem.

Instead we would like a way to disable unsafe-eval behavior without relying on import order. Ideally this is build-time or package-level flag to disable JIT outright. Alternatively, this behavior should be opt-in. I don't think anyone is in good conscience enabling unsafe-eval on production environments. There have been similar proposals in earlier issues, but those were closed without a clear path forward. Could this be reconsidered?

Schema instances have ~91 own properties → dictionary mode → ~24x slower property access vs Zod 3
raw.body:
I'm building a form library that introspects Zod schemas to auto-generate form fields, constraints, and validation. After migrating to Zod 4, I hit a significant introspection performance regression. After a lot of profiling, I tracked the root cause down to schema instance property count.

## The problem

Zod 4 schema instances end up with **~91 own properties**. This pushes them past JS engine fast-property thresholds (V8's is ~27), forcing dictionary mode for all property access — including `_def` and `_zod`.

```javascript
const schema = z.string().min(1).max(10).email();
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(schema).length); // ~91
```

The 91 properties come from:
- **~60** from the core "support prototype modifications" loop that copies prototype methods onto each instance
- **~30** from classic `ZodType` init assigning methods as own properties

Validation perf on valid data is great — this only affects introspection and construction.

## Benchmarks

Property access (same machine, Bun):

| Benchmark | Zod 3 | Zod 4 | Ratio |
|-----------|-------|-------|-------|
| `schema._def` | 298 ps | 7.23 ns | **24x** |
| `schema._zod` | — | 7.2 ns | — |
| Inline extraction | 9.52 ns | 13.08 ns | 1.4x |
| Inline extraction, cached `_zod` | — | 9.2 ns | **parity** |
| `z.string().min(1).max(10).email()` | 2.2 µs | 72.6 µs | **32x** |

Key finding: caching `schema._zod` in a local variable brings per-read performance to Zod 3 parity. The cost is in the initial property lookup on the bloated instance, not in the `_zod` object itself.

<details>
<summary>Real-world impact (form library)</summary>

Cold path (no caching):

| Operation | Zod 3 | Zod 4 | Ratio |
|-----------|-------|-------|-------|
| Field metadata extraction (string+checks) | 7.69M ops/sec | 662K ops/sec | 11.6x |
| Field metadata extraction (number+checks) | 7.26M ops/sec | 961K ops/sec | 7.5x |
| Form mount — simple (5 fields) | 53K ops/sec | 5.8K ops/sec | 9.2x |
| Form mount — complex | 13.1K ops/sec | 1.7K ops/sec | 7.7x |

With WeakMap caching on the warm path, Zod 4 reaches 10.5M ops/sec — actually faster than Zod 3. So it's cacheable, but the cold path and construction cost remain.

</details>

## Reproduction

```javascript
import * as z3 from "zod3"; // zod@3.24.4
import * as z4 from "zod";  // zod@4.x

const v3Schema = z3.string().min(1).max(10).email();
const v4Schema = z4.string().min(1).max(10).email();

// Property count
console.log("Zod 3 own props:", Object.getOwnPropertyNames(v3Schema).length);
console.log("Zod 4 own props:", Object.getOwnPropertyNames(v4Schema).length);

// Property access benchmark
for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) v3Schema._def; // warmup
for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) v4Schema._def;

console.time("Zod 3 _def × 10M");
for (let i = 0; i < 1e7; i++) v3Schema._def;
console.timeEnd("Zod 3 _def × 10M");

console.time("Zod 4 _def × 10M");
for (let i = 0; i < 1e7; i++) v4Schema._def;
console.timeEnd("Zod 4 _def × 10M");

// Construction benchmark
console.time("Zod 3 construction × 10K");
for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) z3.string().min(1).max(10).email();
console.timeEnd("Zod 3 construction × 10K");

console.time("Zod 4 construction × 10K");
for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) z4.string().min(1).max(10).email();
console.timeEnd("Zod 4 construction × 10K");
```

## What I've already tried on my side

- `_def.type` string comparison instead of `instanceof` (instanceof is ~36x slower due to the dual-class chain)
- `_zod.bag` reads instead of iterating `_zod.def.checks` (same path `toJSONSchema` uses)
- `_zod.propValues` for discriminated unions, `_zod.values` for enums
- WeakMap caching of extraction results
- Local `_zod` caching within functions

After all that, the remaining gap is the instance property count — that's the one thing consumers can't fix.

## Workarounds for other library authors hitting this

1. Cache `schema._zod` locally: `const zod = schema._zod` then read `zod.def`, `zod.bag`
2. Use `_zod.bag` for constraints instead of iterating checks
3. Use `_def.type` instead of `instanceof`
4. WeakMap cache extraction results — schemas are immutable so this is safe

## Ideas (not sure what's feasible)

The prototype copy loop is the main contributor (~60 of the 91 properties). I tried removing it but it breaks prototype extension (`prototypes.test.ts`, `apply.test.ts`). Some thoughts:

- Could prototype extension work through a different mechanism (Proxy, `_extensions` map, etc.) that doesn't copy methods to instances?
- Could checks be plain objects instead of `$ZodCheck` class instances? Would reduce construction cost.
- Lazy bag population — only compute on first `_zod.bag` access instead of at construction.

Totally understand if the prototype extension design is intentional and this is a known tradeoff. Just wanted to surface the data in case it's useful.

## Environment

- Zod 4.x, compared against 3.24.4
- Bun (JSC) for benchmarks, also reproduced in Node 22 (V8)

raw.title: Perf: inline field-level validation in generateFastpass (JIT) for further speedups
raw.body:
## Background

While exploring Zod's performance characteristics, I built [zod-aot](https://github.com/wakita181009/zod-aot) — a compiler that inlines runtime validation logic directly into generated code. In benchmarks it shows up to **64x faster** validation compared to Zod v4's JIT.

## Why the gap exists

Zod v4's JIT (`generateFastpass`) is a great improvement — it eliminates the loop over object keys by generating a flat `new Function()`. However, each field's validation still goes through a runtime function call:

```typescript
// Zod v4 JIT — per field
shape["age"]._zod.run({ value: input["age"], issues: [] }, ctx)
```

zod-aot instead inlines the validation logic directly into the generated function body:

```typescript
// zod-aot — per field
if (typeof input["age"] !== "number") { ... }
if (!Number.isSafeInteger(input["age"])) { ... }
```

This eliminates the per-field function call overhead entirely, which is where most of the remaining perf gap comes from.

## Benchmark (Zod v4 JIT-warmed, vitest bench, 500ms warmup + 100 warmup iterations)

| Approach | 7-field object (UserSchema) | Nested object (ApiResponse, 10 items) |
|---|---|---|
| Zod v4 (JIT) | 909,000 ops/sec | 63,000 ops/sec |
| zod-aot | 4,354,000 ops/sec | 2,790,000 ops/sec |
| **Speedup** | **~4.8x** | **~44x** |

## Proposal

Extending `generateFastpass` to emit inlined `typeof` checks for primitive types (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, etc.) — falling back to `_zod.run()` for schemas that can't be statically inlined (e.g. those with custom refinements or transforms) — could bring meaningful performance gains to Zod v4 with no API changes.

This would be a **gold standard** solution: the same speedup zod-aot provides, but built directly into Zod's JIT without requiring any external tooling.

## Role of zod-aot going forward

Even if this is incorporated into Zod's JIT, zod-aot remains useful as a true **AOT (ahead-of-time) compiler** for environments where cold-start cost is unacceptable (e.g. edge functions, Cloudflare Workers) — since it requires no `new Function()` at runtime and is therefore also CSP-safe.
